title: Infusion-Set Change Rate — Clinical Supply Allowance Guide, Insulin Pump Program
content:
On an Insulin Pump Program the set rate of an infusion-set refill — the infusion sets allowed per 30 days — follows the customer's dispensing on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program, that is, on the customer's active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump. Its pump insulin item is J1817 on the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program and rapid-acting 10 mL vials on any other tier.

## Allowance rule

1. **Pump insulin item dispensed in the last six months.** Where the customer holds an active pump-delivery insulin pharmacy program and its pump insulin item was dispensed under it in the six months before the ship date, the standard set rate is replaced with the set changes the daily pump insulin needs: 30 times the daily pump insulin divided by the cartridge fill for the pump, rounded up to a whole set and never fewer than 10 sets per 30 days (the standard sets per 30 days).
2. **Such a program, but the item not dispensed in six months.** Where the customer holds such a program but that item was not dispensed under it in those six months, the standard set rate is replaced with the previous infusion-set refill's sets times 30 divided by its supply days, rounded up, and stands where there is no previous infusion-set refill.
3. **Otherwise** the standard set rate stands.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Case | Set rate |
|---|---|
| Daily pump insulin 110 units, cartridge fill 300 units | 30 times 110 is 3,300; divided by 300 is 11 sets per 30 days |
| Daily pump insulin 50 units, cartridge fill 200 units | 1,500 divided by 200 is 7.5, rounded up to 8; held at the floor of 10 sets |
| Item not dispensed in six months; previous infusion-set refill of 33 sets over 90 days | 990 divided by 90 is 11 sets per 30 days |
| Item not dispensed in six months; no previous infusion-set refill | the standard set rate stands |
